conventions.convention: Signals and data are finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces; the correction is Aᵀ(y−Ax). Deployment parameters are fixed, depth N≥1, and layers are indexed from 0 through N−1.

Layer domains use relative product sigma-algebras; initialization and updates are Borel. The recursive admissible domain includes exactly inputs where every update is defined. The measurability lemma also permits N=0.

Automatic differentiation concerns the finite deployed map, with complete deterministic primitives and derivative rules. Piecewise primitives require a unique strict branch on an open neighborhood; no derivative is asserted at branch boundaries.
Risk comparisons use a common nonempty Borel evaluation space E contained in every compared deployment domain, squared signal loss, and joint input-target laws on E×X.
The Landweber example assumes Countable Choice, exact data with δ=0, a>0, nonzero truth, and 0<ωa²<1. Its finite residual remains positive, so it returns at budget exhaustion.

load_bearing.statement: Then every E_k is a Borel subset of Ω and every x_k:E_k→X is Borel. In particular, E_N is exactly the set of inputs where all N updates are defined, and the finite output map x_N:E_N→X is Borel.

A depth-N architecture has Borel initialization and Borel update maps on declared Borel domains, with x_{k+1}=B_{θ_k}((A,y),x_k+τ_kAᵀ(y−Ax_k)); its deployed output is the finite composition on its admissible domain, with parameters held fixed at deployment.

Finite evaluability does not imply convergence of an infinite continuation. Zero finite training risk alone yields no uniform shifted residual or squared test-risk bound. Under the stated differentiability assumptions, automatic differentiation computes the finite-map derivative; even zero fixed-point residual need not make it equal the fixed-point derivative.
